items.q: What does AVRIX Digital actually do?
items.a: We help UK and European organisations do four things: find security gaps before attackers do, watch for attacks around the clock, prove they're protected (Cyber Essentials, ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, PCI DSS, NIS2 and DORA), and recover quickly when something goes wrong.

items.q: What size of organisation do you work with?
items.a: Anything from a 10-person firm with its first customer questionnaire to large, regulated groups. Typical clients are in finance, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, software, the public sector, charities and education.

items.q: Who will we be working with?
items.a: Everything is delivered by AVRIX Digital with our specialist team. You sign one contract, have one named contact and deal with one team that is accountable for the outcome.

items.q: How soon can a test start?
items.a: A scoping call can usually happen within a few working days. Once scope and written permission are signed off, we book the testing window, and urgent work goes to the front of the queue.

items.q: Could testing knock our systems over?
items.a: We plan specifically to avoid that. We agree time windows, keep traffic under control and don't use anything destructive without your say-so. Fragile or critical systems can be tested out of hours or on a copy.
Yes. Once you've fixed the issues we check them again and update the report, so you have a clean version to share with customers or auditors.

items.q: Is it legal to hack our own systems?
items.a: It is when the owner has authorised it in writing. Unauthorised access is a crime under the UK Computer Misuse Act 1990 and equivalent laws across Europe, which is why nothing starts until scope and permission are signed.

items.q: Which certification should we go for first?
items.a: In the UK, Cyber Essentials is the usual first step and is required for many public sector contracts. ISO 27001 carries the most weight with UK and European buyers, while US customers tend to ask for SOC 2. We'll suggest a route based on who's asking.

items.q: Do NIS2 and DORA affect UK companies?
items.a: Not directly, as they're EU laws. However, UK firms offering covered services in the EU can be in scope, and EU customers increasingly pass NIS2 or DORA obligations down through supplier contracts. The UK is also strengthening its own NIS Regulations.

No, and no consultant should. Certificates come from independent, accredited bodies: IASME-licensed certification bodies for Cyber Essentials and UKAS-accredited bodies for ISO 27001. We get you ready and stay with you through the audit.

items.q: Isn't 24/7 monitoring overkill for a smaller business?
items.a: Not necessarily. Smaller organisations are attractive precisely because nobody is watching overnight. We price monitoring by users and systems, so it scales down as well as up.

items.q: Where will our data be kept?
items.a: We agree this before onboarding. For UK and EU clients, monitoring data can stay in UK or EU hosting regions to support UK GDPR and EU GDPR obligations.

items.q: We think we've been attacked. What now?
items.a: Unplug affected devices from the network but leave them powered on. Don't delete files, pay a ransom or reply to the attackers. Then contact us and mark the enquiry urgent. If personal data could be involved, the ICO or your EU regulator may need to be told within 72 hours.

items.q: Can you help before anything happens?
items.a: Yes, and it's far cheaper than responding unprepared. We write response plans and ransomware playbooks, check that backups actually restore and run rehearsals with your leadership team.

Projects such as testing and certification support are quoted at a fixed price after a free scoping call. Ongoing services are a monthly fee based on users and systems. Incident support is available on demand or through a retainer.

items.q: Will you sign a confidentiality agreement?
items.a: Yes. We can sign yours or offer a mutual NDA before you share anything sensitive.

items.q: What happens to our data during the work?
items.a: We only touch what the agreed scope needs, use test accounts wherever we can, keep findings in secure storage and delete engagement data once it's no longer required, in line with our contract and data protection law.
